alignments.note: The verb keeps only its own lexical word; its English subject has gone to the expressed nominative quantifier, which is present and unspent.

The supplied *they* belongs to the expressed nominative quantifier, not to the verb. Rule 9's licence to give an inflected verb an English subject is for a subject Greek leaves unexpressed; here πάντες stands and is not spent elsewhere, so rule 76's availability test makes it the word the pronoun belongs to, and rule 7 keeps the helper with what licenses it. This is the same expansion of a substantival πᾶς that the chapter reads at 6:30 πάντα → *all things* and 6:41 πᾶσιν → *among them all*, and rule 17's generic-completion clause holds the head on the quantifier. Aligned as at 6:50, where the identical πάντες plus finite verb takes *they all* on the quantifier. Giving *they* to ἔφαγον under rule 9 is the competing reading; it was the chapter's own earlier one, and it forces the verb to straddle *all* discontinuously for no gain.
Inflected verb takes its auxiliary; head on the lexical verb (rule 9).

review_notes: Reconciled to MRK.6.50: the supplied *they* rides with the expressed nominative πάντες, headed on *all*.
The verb-headed reading is named in the unit's note as the competing one, per rule 16.
